help.intro: Like sein and haben, the modal verbs go into the simple past rather than the Perfekt when you talk about the past: Ich konnte nicht kommen (I couldn't come), Ich musste arbeiten (I had to work), Er wollte schlafen (he wanted to sleep). Nobody says 'ich habe kommen können' in everyday speech. The forms are regular and easy: the stem loses its umlaut (können → konn-, müssen → muss-, dürfen → durf-), takes -te, and adds the past endings: konnte, konntest, konnte, konnten, konntet, konnten. The main verb stays an infinitive at the end, exactly as in the present. With war and hatte they are almost the whole Präteritum of everyday speech.
help.tips[0].title: Stem without umlaut + -te + endings
help.tips[0].text: konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte, mochte. Endings: -te, -test, -te, -ten, -tet, -ten. ich and er identical, as always in the past.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I couldn't come yesterday, I had to work.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We wanted to go to the cinema, but we weren't allowed.
help.tips[0].check.q: Wir ____ gestern lange auf den Bus warten.
help.tips[0].check.why: wir takes the ending -ten: wir mussten. musste is for ich and er, musstet for ihr.
help.tips[1].title: Infinitive still at the end
help.tips[1].text: The bracket is unchanged: modal at 2, infinitive last. Ich | musste | gestern lange | arbeiten.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: She was supposed to be there at eight.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: We had to work late yesterday.
help.tips[1].check.why: The modal stays in position 2 and the infinitive goes to the very end, just like in the present.
help.tips[2].title: No Perfekt for modals in speech
help.tips[2].text: 'Ich habe nicht kommen können' exists but is heavy and rare. Say ich konnte nicht kommen. Same for sein/haben: war, hatte.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Why didn't you come? – I couldn't.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: We wanted to go to the cinema, but we weren't allowed to.
help.tips[2].trap: the modals, sein and haben are the three groups that avoid the Perfekt. Everything else uses it.
help.tips[2].check.q: Which is the natural way to say „I couldn't come yesterday“?
help.tips[2].check.options[1]: Ich habe gestern nicht gekonnt kommen.
help.tips[2].check.options[2]: Ich bin gestern nicht kommen gekonnt.
help.tips[2].check.why: In speech, modals use the simple past — konnte — instead of the Perfekt.
help.tips[3].title: The umlaut goes
help.tips[3].text: können → konnte, müssen → musste, dürfen → durfte, mögen → mochte. wollen and sollen had none to lose: wollte, sollte.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: As a child I didn't like spinach.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: As a child I wasn't allowed to watch TV for long.
help.tips[3].check.q: Als Kind ____ ich nicht allein in die Stadt fahren. (wasn't allowed)
help.tips[3].check.why: The umlaut goes in the past: dürfen → durfte. dürfte with the umlaut means 'might'.
help.remember[0]: Drop the umlaut, add -te: konnte, musste, durfte.
help.remember[1]: war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte: the five past forms spoken German uses most.
help.context.en: Yesterday I wanted to go to a concert with friends, but I couldn't: I had to work until eight. My boss said I was to finish a report. And my colleague was allowed to leave early – she had an appointment. As a child I wanted to become a musician. And you, what did you want to become?
help.mistakes[0].why: könnte (with umlaut) is 'could' as in 'would be able'; the past is konnte.
help.mistakes[1].why: Modals use the Präteritum in speech.
help.hook: „Ich konnte nicht, ich musste arbeiten“ — the past-tense excuse everyone needs, built from a few short, regular forms.
englishTemplates.können → konnte[1]: {subject} could swim well as a child.
englishTemplates.wollen → wollte[0]: {subject} wanted to go to the cinema.
englishTemplates.dürfen → durfte[0]: {subject} was not allowed to watch TV.
englishTemplates.dürfen → durfte[1]: As a child {subject} was allowed to play for a long time.
englishTemplates.sollen → sollte[0]: {subject} was supposed to do the homework.
englishTemplates.sollen → sollte[1]: {subject} was supposed to be there at eight.
